newsitem.title: USA: Ill. House to hear electric deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Ill. House to hear electric deregulation bill.

text.p: An Illinois House committee has advanced an electric utility deregulation bill that is expected to be considered by representatives in a session on Friday afternoon, a spokesman for the House leadership said.

The House electric utility deregulation committee voted Thursday to advance the long-debated 300-plus page plan to the House floor for consideration when lawmakers meet beginning at 1400 EDT, said Steve Brown, spokesman for House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago.
Mesirow Financial analyst Catherina Milostan said researchers expect the House to vote Friday on the deregulation plan, possibly followed by a Senate vote on Saturday.

"We believe the past few days' revisions addresses many of the governor's previously expressed concerns and have furthered the process," Milostan said in a statement. "However, many industrial associations remain in the opposition favoring further changes. We expect the debate to remain heated right up until the House vote."
Gov. Jim Edgar has said he had a number of concerns about details in the bill and could use an amendatory veto power if necessary to order changes in the plan.

The deregulation plan is supported by Commonwealth Edison, a subsidiary of Unicom Corp; Illinois Power Co, a subsidiary of Illinova Corp; CIPSCO; the Citizens Utility Board; the Illinois Retail Merchants Association; and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers.
The plan would cost ComEd an estimated $1.6 billion over three years beginning in 1998, spokeswoman Marjorie Benzkofer said.
Central Illinois Light, a subsidiary of CILCORP, and the Illinois Manufacturer's Assocation remain opposed to the plan.
CUB's support of the plan marks a shift for the longtime adversary of utilities and shows that the issues may be reaching a consensus, Milostan indicated in a research report.
The plan advanced to the House floor includes 10 percent rate reductions in 1998 for ComEd and Illinois Power customers, followed by another 5 percent reduction in October 2000.
CIPSCO and CILCO customers would see a 5 percent reduction in 1998 and 5 percent decreases in October 2000 and October 2002 if rates rise above the midwest average.

The plan had called for phasing in customer choice for utilities through 2003, but amendments to the bill in recent days would speed that process, giving all residents access by 2002 and all commercial/industrial customers by the year 2000, Benzkofer said.
